16.name: sleeps well enough
16.description: She sleeps better than she has since the Serrano file arrived, though not perfectly.
evidence: She did not, that night, sleep badly.
She slept the way she had used to sleep before the Serrano file had come into her office

16.name: wakes at six
16.description: She wakes up at six in the morning.
evidence: She woke at six.

16.name: makes morning coffee
16.description: She prepares coffee as part of her morning routine.
evidence: She made coffee.

16.name: prepares for new client intake
16.description: At her kitchen table, she begins organizing notes for a new client scheduled to come in at nine.
evidence: She sat at her kitchen table with a fresh pad of paper and a fresh pen and she wrote, at the top, the name of a new client, whose intake was scheduled for nine

16.name: notes difficult family warning
16.description: She records that the new client's family has been described as difficult and marks the word for emphasis.
evidence: whose family, she had been told by the referring attorney, was difficult, and she underlined the word *difficult*
and then, after a moment, crossed out the underline

16.name: reframes difficult families
16.description: She reflects that difficult estates often use that label to intimidate handlers and that the hardest-looking families may simply be afraid.
evidence: she had learned, over the last six weeks, that *difficult* was a word that estates threw at the people who handled them in order to scare them away from doing the work properly
and that the families who looked the most difficult from the outside were often the families who, on the inside, were most afraid that no one would help them tell the truth

16.name: walks to the office
16.description: She leaves home and goes to her office.
evidence: She drank her coffee. She walked to the office.

16.name: opens new file
16.description: She opens the new case file at the office.
evidence: She opened the new file.

16.name: files Serrano codicil
16.description: The original codicil is filed with the Register of Wills, copied into Asha's closed-estates binder, and shelved in her office.
evidence: The codicil, in its original form, with Rosa's signature on it as a witness and Mrs. Serrano's signature on it in the careful slow handwriting of a woman who had taken her time, was filed in the Register of Wills office in Philadelphia and assigned a number
and a copy of it was placed in the binder Asha kept for closed estates, and the binder was placed on a shelf in her office
16.location_hint: Register of Wills office in Philadelphia / Asha's office

16.name: estate is filed and archived
16.description: The closed estate is registered in the Philadelphia Register of Wills office, assigned a number, and filed away in Asha's binder among other closed estates.
evidence: gister of Wills office in Philadelphia and assigned a number, and a copy of it was placed in the binder Asha kept for closed estates, and the binder was placed on a shelf in her office between two other binders of two other estates
16.location_hint: Register of Wills office in Philadelphia

16.name: Spruce Street house remains occupied
16.description: The house on Spruce Street continues as a lived-in home with Lucia and Rosa still residing there.
evidence: The house on Spruce Street remained a house. Lucia lived in it. Rosa lived on the third floor.

16.name: Daniel resumes Sunday visits
16.description: Daniel begins visiting the house on Sunday afternoons, initially awkwardly and then with more ease.
evidence: Daniel visited, at first awkwardly and then less awkwardly, on Sunday afternoons

16.name: Daniel brings kind girlfriend
16.description: By spring, Daniel brings a woman he is seeing, and Lucia learns she is kind to Rosa.
evidence: and brought, by the spring, a woman he was seeing, who was kind to Rosa, which Lucia reported to Asha over coffee as the single most useful piece of information she had received about her brother in fifteen years.

16.name: Lucia reports useful news to Asha
16.description: Lucia tells Asha over coffee that Daniel's girlfriend is kind to Rosa, treating it as the most useful information she has learned about him in years.
evidence: which Lucia reported to Asha over coffee as the single most useful piece of information she had received about her brother in fifteen years

16.name: property charge is paid down
16.description: The debt on the property is reduced according to Asha's repayment schedule.
evidence: The charge on the property was paid down on the schedule Asha had drafted

16.name: property is paid off early
16.description: In the third year, the property is paid off ahead of schedule after Lucia's New York apartment sells for more than expected and she realizes she does not miss it.
evidence: and then, in the third year, paid off early, because Lucia's apartment in New York had sold for more than she had expected and because she found that she did not, in fact, miss it.

16.name: Lucia keeps letter in bedroom drawer
16.description: Lucia stores the letter she found in her bedroom drawer and rereads it on bad days without showing it to Daniel.
evidence: The letter Lucia had found in the sewing room, the one she had given to Asha and that Asha had given back to her, lived in a drawer in Lucia's bedroom, which had been her mother's bedroom, and Lucia read it, on the bad days, and put it back.
She did not show it to Daniel.

16.name: Lucia accepts letter's purpose
16.description: Lucia recognizes that the letter has already accomplished what it was meant to do and is now just an ordinary piece of paper.
evidence: The letter had done its work in the moment it had been written and again in the moment it had been read, and what it had asked Lucia to do, Lucia had done, and the letter was now simply a piece of paper

16.name: Rosa's letter continues helping Lucia
16.description: The letter Rosa wrote has already done its work and still helps Lucia on bad days.
evidence: had done its work in the moment it had been written and again in the moment it had been read, and what it had asked Lucia to do, Lucia had done, and the letter was now simply a piece of paper that her mother had once held in her hands and that, on the bad days, helped.

16.name: Rosa lives in the house for nine more years
16.description: Rosa remains living in the house for another nine years after the letter's effect.
evidence: Rosa lived in the house for another nine years.

16.name: Rosa dies in her sleep
16.description: Rosa dies peacefully in the third-floor room she chose.
evidence: She died in her sleep, in the third-floor room she had chosen, on a Tuesday in October

16.name: Lucia finds Rosa dead
16.description: In the morning, Lucia discovers Rosa's body and begins calling for help.
evidence: Lucia found her in the morning and called Daniel and then called Asha

16.name: Asha arrives as a friend
16.description: Asha comes over to support Lucia and Daniel personally rather than in her professional role.
evidence: Asha came over, not as the attorney, because Rosa had a different attorney by then, a friend of Asha's whom Asha had recommended when Rosa had decided, at seventy-five, to put her own affairs in order, but as a friend

16.name: They wait in the kitchen after Rosa's death
16.description: Lucia, Daniel, and Asha sit in the kitchen drinking coffee and waiting for the authorities to arrive.
evidence: she sat in the kitchen with Lucia and Daniel and they drank coffee and waited for the people who had to come

16.name: Lucia says Rosa wanted to be there
16.description: Lucia expresses that Rosa had wanted to remain in the house until the end.
evidence: Lucia said, at one point, "She wanted to be here,"

16.name: Daniel affirms Rosa was there
16.description: Daniel responds that Rosa was indeed present in the house in the meaningful sense.
evidence: and Daniel said, "She was here,"

16.name: Asha reflects on the work's purpose
16.description: Asha silently realizes that preserving the house and its people was the point of her work.
evidence: Asha said nothing, because there was nothing to say
that, Asha thought, sitting in the kitchen of a house she had once helped to keep from being sold, was what the work had been for

16.name: Asha leaves the kitchen
16.description: After finishing her coffee, Asha stands up and puts her cup in the sink.
evidence: She finished her coffee. She got up. She put her cup in the sink

16.name: reflects on the work's purpose
16.description: Asha sits in the kitchen and realizes that the work she has done here was meant to preserve the house and family.
evidence: that, Asha thought, sitting in the kitchen of a house she had once helped to keep from being sold, was what the work had been for.

16.name: finishes coffee and stands up
16.description: Asha finishes her coffee and gets up from the kitchen table.
evidence: She finished her coffee. She got up.

16.name: rinses cup as taught by Rosa
16.description: Asha rinses her cup and puts it upside down on the rack, following Rosa's old instruction that marked her as part of the house rather than a guest.
evidence: She put her cup in the sink, the way Rosa had taught her, the first time she had ever stayed for lunch, by simply taking the cup out of her hand and rinsing it and setting it upside down on the rack and not saying anything about it, which had been Rosa's way of saying, *you are not a guest here anymore, you are a person, and persons rinse their cups.* She rinsed it now. She set it upside down on the rack.

16.name: returns to sit with Lucia and Daniel
16.description: Asha goes back into the dining room and sits across from Lucia and Daniel, resuming the shared waiting that defines her role.
evidence: Then she went back into the dining room, where Lucia and Daniel were sitting on the same side of the table, the way they had sat that Monday morning years ago, and she sat down across from them, at the place where she had sat the day they had closed the estate, and she waited with them, because waiting with people was, in the end, the largest part of what she did, and the part she had become, over a long career that had begun in earnest in this house, best at.

16.name: house shelters the gathered family
16.description: The house is described as holding Asha, Lucia, Daniel, and the family history they embody, suggesting its enduring protective role.
evidence: The house held them, as it had held the woman who had built her family inside it and the woman who had kept that family running and the two children who had not always known what to do with either of them, and it would, Asha thought, hold them a whil
participants: the woman who had built her family inside it
the woman who had kept that family running

16.name: reflect on house's temporary shelter
16.description: Asha reflects that the house has held her family and the woman who kept it running, and that it can only be expected to shelter them for a while longer.
evidence: had built her family inside it and the woman who had kept that family running and the two children who had not always known what to do with either of them, and it would, Asha thought, hold them a while longer, which was all any house was ever asked to do

16.name: consider limits of house paperwork
16.description: Asha thinks about the people who handle house paperwork and the limited promises they can honestly make.
evidence: and all any of the people who worked on the paperwork of houses could ever, honestly, promise
participants: people who worked on the paperwork of houses

16.name: sit with friends and wait
16.description: Asha sits with her friends and waits for the people who are supposed to arrive.
evidence: She sat with her friends and waited for the people who had to come.
participants: the people who had to come

16.name: morning continues outside
16.description: The morning keeps moving on outside while Asha waits.
evidence: Outside, the morning went on.
